answer: Submissions that land within 142 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The cedar detector writes to cipher, and forge makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 140 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 35 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
